    Urban Program

    On this page

          The Urban Maintenance Program distributes more than $600M in annual funding to 85 urban localities to help them maintain nearly 27,000 lane miles of roadway infrastructure. The program ensures financial accountability by collecting and analyzing annual financial reports and monitors roadway conditions by conducting inspections of locally maintained arterial streets.

          As established in Section 33.2-319 of the Code of Virginia, the Urban Maintenance Program oversees Commonwealth Transportation Board (CTB) payments to cities and towns in the urban system for maintenance, construction, and reconstruction of highways that meet specific criteria and conditions.

          There are currently 85 localities in the urban system. A municipality qualifies for the urban program if it meets any of the following criteria:

          • All cities, regardless of population
          • All incorporated towns of more than 3,500 population, according to the latest U.S. Census or other documented evidence
          • The towns of Chase City, Elkton, Grottoes, Narrows, Pearisburg, Saltville, Altavista, Dublin, Lebanon and Wise

          Virginia Administrative Code 24VAC30-325-10 outlines additional eligibility criteria and requirements for the urban program, including the establishment of administrative procedures in the Urban Manual.

          Urban Manual

          Provides unified policies and procedures to help VDOT staff and urban localities deliver programs that meet state and federal requirements.

          Urban Mileage Payments

          View VDOT’s FY27 mileage payment schedule showing per lane-mile rates and the quarterly and annual allocation amounts for urban arterials and local streets.

          History of Payment Rates

          Access VDOT’s FY86–FY27 payment-rate history table detailing urban arterials/collectors and Henrico/Arlington County lane-mile rates.

          Road Inventory

          List of locally maintained streets which receive maintenance payments.

          Inventory Change Request

          Use UICR to submit municipal street inventory updates for VDOT maintenance payments, ensuring all required materials meet program standards.

          Maintenance Eligibility Tool

          Identify eligible maintenance activities using a tool aligned with the U‑3 Survey and VDOT reporting to determine which tasks qualify for Urban Maintenance funding.

          Roadway Maintenance

          Eligibility 

          Not all maintenance activities qualify for Urban Maintenance Program funding. You can find a full list of eligible and ineligible activities in the Maintenance Eligibility Tool. Each activity includes the category it should be assigned to for the Highway Finance Survey.

          Maintenance Eligibility Tool

          Accounting

          To help urban localities align their maintenance expenditure reporting with the Highway Finance Survey, Local Assistance developed an accounting template.

          Urban Maintenance Fund Accounting Template for Localities

          Expenditure Reports

          Urban localities must report their maintenance expenditures to VDOT each year. They submit this information via an annual VDOT-administered survey. The survey, distributed to localities by December, must be completed using audited financial data. The Virginia Code also requires urban localities to report on the performance of their systems.

          Highway Finance Survey Instructions

          Equipment Rental Rates

          Localities develop their own equipment rental rates. If localities have not developed rates, we recommend using commercially available rates via the Rental Rate Blue Book. For declared emergencies only, the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) equipment rates may be used. The cost of the Rental Rate Blue Book purchase is an eligible expense for using maintenance funds.

          Rental Rate Blue Book

          FEMA Equipment Rates 

          Inventory

          Inventory Changes 

          Each year, the CTB approves mileage additions and deletions and authorizes payments to localities in the urban system. Localities are responsible for updating the Urban Inventory. Changes can be made using the Urban Inventory Change Request application. Change requests are due February 1st to be included in the following fiscal year.

          Urban Inventory Change Request

          Arterial Inspections

          Arterial pavement inspections are conducted annually by VDOT staff. Information on the condition of bridges in the urban system is included in the maintenance section of VDOT’s Dashboard.

          Payments

          Locality Payments 

          The Commissioner of Highways, with approval from the CTB, provides payments to cities and certain towns for maintaining eligible highways. These payments are based on the number of moving-lane-miles of highways, or portions of highways, available to peak-hour traffic within each locality.

          FY27 Urban Municipal Mileage Payments

          Evaluation of City Street Conditions Final Report

          Best Practices for Records Retention

          Overweight Permit Fee

          In accordance with §§ 46.2-1140.1, 46.2-1143, 46.2-1148, and 46.2-1149.1 of the Code of Virginia beginning in Fiscal Year 2014, overweight permit fee revenue is distributed on the basis of lane mileage to localities along with their quarterly maintenance payments.

          FY27 Urban Permit Fee Payment

          Related Programs

          Urban Counties

          Unlike other counties in Virginia, Arlington and Henrico counties have withdrawn from the secondary state highway system and maintain their system of local roads.

          Section 33.2-366 of the Code of Virginia sets out the process for determining the amount that the state pays these counties for the maintenance of their local road systems annually.

          The 2013 General Assembly established a new base amount for maintenance of $17,218 per lane-mile for Arlington and $12,529 per lane-mile for Henrico. These amounts are then adjusted annually to account for inflation by multiplying the annual rate per category, using the base rate of growth planned for the VDOT's highway maintenance and operations program.

          Guide for County Road Systems in Arlington and Henrico counties

          FY27 Arlington County Allocation Worksheet

          FY27 Henrico County Allocation Worksheet 

          FY27 County Overweight Permit Fee Revenue

          State of Good Repair

          State of Good Repair

          The State of Good Repair (SGR) program provides additional funding to help restore pavement and bridge assets that have deteriorated beyond normal maintenance levels, using a needs-based distribution of funding. SGR serves as a supplemental source of support when roadway conditions fall below acceptable standards. SGR funding complements but does not replace quarterly maintenance funds.
